questions.q: After the fall of the Guptas, different kingdoms emerged in various parts of India. Among them, the Maukharis emerged in which of the following areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kannauj.

Key Points

• The Maukharis were an ancient Indian dynasty that ruled over parts of northern India after the decline of the Gupta Empire.

• They initially served as vassals of the Guptas before establishing their independent rule.

• The Maukharis made Kannauj their capital, which later became a prominent center of power and culture in northern India.

• Kannauj, under the Maukharis, became an important political, economic, and cultural hub during their reign.

Additional Information

• Maukharis Dynasty:

• The Maukharis were initially feudatories of the Guptas but later established their own independent rule in northern India.

• They ruled over the region that includes parts of present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

• Key rulers of the Maukhari dynasty include Hari-varman and Aditya-varman.

• Kannauj:

• Kannauj is an ancient city in Uttar Pradesh, known for its historical and cultural significance.

• It became a major center of power during the rule of various dynasties, including the Maukharis, Harshavardhanas, and the Gurjara-Pratiharas.

• During the medieval period, Kannauj was a key battleground for dominance over northern India.

• Gupta Empire:

• The Gupta Empire was one of the largest and most powerful empires in ancient India, known for its advancements in arts, science, and political administration.

• It existed approximately from the 4th to the 6th century CE and is often referred to as the Golden Age of India.

• Key rulers include Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II.

questions.q: Presently, which of the following countries is NOT a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme?

The correct answer is Angola.

Key Points

• The Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme was introduced by the Government of India in 2008.

• The scheme aims to provide market access at zero duty to products originating from Least Developed Countries (LDCs).

• Rwanda, Burundi, and Myanmar are some of the beneficiaries of the DFTP Scheme.

• Angola is currently not a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme.

Additional Information

• Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme

• The DFTP Scheme was launched by India to provide preferential market access for goods originating from Least Developed Countries (LDCs).

• The main objective is to enhance South-South cooperation and contribute to the development of LDCs.

• The scheme covers around 98% of tariff lines, making a wide range of products from LDCs eligible for zero-duty benefits.

• It has the potential to significantly boost exports from LDCs to India, thereby supporting their economic growth and development.

• LDCs are a group of countries that are recognized by the United Nations as being the most disadvantaged in terms of their low gross national income, weak human assets, and economic vulnerability.

• As of October 2023, there are 46 countries classified as LDCs.

• LDCs benefit from various international support measures, including preferential market access and development assistance.

• The aim is to help these countries overcome structural challenges, eradicate poverty, and achieve sustainable development.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 80.

Key Points

• Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Council of States, which is commonly known as the Rajya Sabha.

• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Parliament of India.

• As per Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than 250 members.

• Out of these, 12 members are nominated by the President of India from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service, and the remaining members are representatives of the States and Union territories.

Additional Information

• Article 76

• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the office of the Attorney General of India.

• The Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and has the right to participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament, but without a right to vote.

• Article 84

• Article 84 of the Indian Constitution specifies the qualifications required to be a member of Parliament.

• These qualifications include being a citizen of India, being not less than 30 years of age in the case of the Rajya Sabha and 25 years in the case of the Lok Sabha, and possessing such other qualifications as may be prescribed by law by the Parliament.

• Article 92

• Article 92 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

• It states that while the office of Chairman or Deputy Chairman is vacant, or in the absence of the Chairman from any sitting of the Council, the duties of the office shall be performed by the Deputy Chairman, or if the Deputy Chairman is also absent, by such member of the Council as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the Council.

questions.q: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Opposite.

Key Points

• In an opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves arise at the same level from opposite sides of the stem.

• Each pair of leaves is typically perpendicular to the next pair above or below, providing a crisscross pattern.

• Opposite phyllotaxy ensures maximum light exposure for each leaf, which is beneficial for photosynthesis.

• This type of leaf arrangement is common in plants such as guava (Psidium guajava), calotropis, and jamun.

Additional Information

• Phyllotaxy

• Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of leaves on a plant stem.

• The primary types of phyllotaxy are alternate, opposite, and whorled.

• This arrangement plays a significant role in maximizing light capture and minimizing shading of lower leaves.

• Alternate Phyllotaxy

• In alternate phyllotaxy, each leaf arises at a different level on the stem, and the leaves are not directly opposite each other.

• Examples include sunflower and mustard.

• Whorled Phyllotaxy

• In whorled phyllotaxy, three or more leaves grow at the same level around the stem.

• This arrangement is less common and can be seen in plants like Nerium (oleander).

questions.q: Which of following is NOT a device of parliamentary proceedings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Full-day discussion.

Key Points

• Full-day discussion is not a recognized device of parliamentary proceedings in India.

• Indian Parliament has specific mechanisms for discussions such as Half-an-hour discussion, Zero-hour discussion, and Two-hour (short) discussion.

• These mechanisms are structured to ensure organized and efficient proceedings within the Parliament.

• The concept of a "Full-day discussion" does not exist as a formal parliamentary procedure in India.

Additional Information

• Half-an-hour discussion

• It is a device in the Indian Parliament where members can raise a matter of public importance, which requires an oral answer from the concerned minister.

• This discussion takes place for half an hour, typically at the end of the day's session.

• It allows members to seek clarification on specific issues from the ministers.

• Zero-hour discussion

• It is an informal device available to the members of the Indian Parliament to raise matters without any prior notice.

• It starts immediately after the Question Hour and lasts until the agenda for the day is taken up.

• Members can raise urgent matters of public importance during this time.

• Two-hour (short) discussion

• This device allows for a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for a duration of two hours.

• No formal motion is moved and no voting takes place at the end of the discussion.

• The aim is to allow members to express their views and enable the government to clarify its position on the issue.

questions.q: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Philips curve.

Key Points

• The Philips curve represents the inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.

• The concept was first introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958.

• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy leads to higher wages, which in turn leads to higher inflation.

• This relationship suggests that policymakers face a trade-off between reducing unemployment and controlling inflation.

Additional Information

• Friedman's Model

• Also known as the Monetarist Theory, it was proposed by Milton Friedman.

• Friedman argued that there is no long-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment, as suggested by the Phillips curve.

• He introduced the concept of the Natural Rate of Unemployment, which posits that the economy will always revert to this natural rate despite short-term fluctuations.

• Friedman emphasized the role of monetary policy in controlling inflation.

• Keynesian Model

• Developed by John Maynard Keynes, this model emphasizes total spending in the economy (aggregate demand) and its effects on output and inflation.

• Keynesians advocate for active government intervention to manage economic cycles.

• They believe that insufficient demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.

• In contrast to the Phillips curve, Keynesians may support policies that increase aggregate demand to reduce unemployment without necessarily causing high inflation.

• Baumol Hypothesis

• Proposed by economist William J. Baumol, it addresses the cost disease in service sectors.

• Baumol's hypothesis suggests that wages in labor-intensive sectors (like services) rise due to wage increases in other sectors that experience higher productivity growth.

• This leads to higher costs in the service sector without corresponding increases in productivity.

• The hypothesis is often used to explain rising costs in sectors such as healthcare and education.

• When an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, the rays after refraction through the lens become parallel to each other.

• Thus, the image formed will be at infinity on the right side of the lens.

Additional Information

• A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges and is also known as a converging lens because it converges light rays that are initially parallel.

• It is used in various optical devices such as magnifying glasses, cameras, and corrective lenses for farsightedness.

• The focus (or focal point) of a lens is the point where parallel light rays converge (for a convex lens) or appear to diverge from (for a concave lens).

• The distance from the lens to the focus is called the focal length.

• Image Formation by Convex Lens:

• When an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, the refracted rays become parallel, indicating that the image is formed at infinity.

• When the object is placed between the lens and the focus, the image formed is virtual, erect, and enlarged.

questions.q: A circle's centre is connected to its 50 cm long chord by a perpendicular that is 21 cm long. Find the circle's radius.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Half of the chord = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm.

The radius, perpendicular, and half-chord form a right-angled triangle.

Radius = √(perpendicular² + half-chord²)

Radius = √(21² + 25²) = √(441 + 625) = √1066 cm.

∴ The correct answer is √1066 cm.

Calculations:

⇒ AM = MB = AB ÷ 2

⇒ Applying Pythagoras theorem in ΔOMA:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ r² = 21² + 25²

⇒ r² = 441 + 625

⇒ r = √1066 cm

∴ The correct answer is √1066 cm.

Perpendicular to a Chord Property

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to any chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments. Conversely, a line joining the centre and the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.

Shortcut Trick

Factorize the numerator using substitution: 25a² − 10ab − 48b² = (5a − 8b)(5a + 6b).

Divide by the denominator (5a + 6b) to get (5a − 8b).

Multiply the result by (5a + 8b).

Apply algebraic identity (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y² ⇒ (5a − 8b)(5a + 8b) = 25a² − 64b².

∴ The correct answer is 25a² − 64b².

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: [(25a² − 10ab − 48b²) ÷ (5a + 6b)] × (5a + 8b)

Splitting the middle term for quadratic factorization.

Difference of squares: (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y²

Calculations:

⇒ Split the middle term of the numerator 25a² − 10ab − 48b².

⇒ Find two numbers that multiply to (25 × −48) = −1200 and add to −10.

⇒ The numbers are −40 and +30.

⇒ 25a² − 40ab + 30ab − 48b²

⇒ 5a(5a − 8b) + 6b(5a − 8b)

⇒ (5a − 8b)(5a + 6b)

⇒ Substitute the factors back into the given expression:

⇒ [(5a − 8b)(5a + 6b) ÷ (5a + 6b)] × (5a + 8b)

⇒ The term (5a + 6b) cancels out from the numerator and denominator.

⇒ Remaining expression: (5a − 8b) × (5a + 8b)

⇒ Apply the difference of squares formula:

⇒ (5a)² − (8b)² = 25a² − 64b²

∴ The correct answer is 25a² − 64b².

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities

Rule of Alligation

It allows us to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture at a desired price: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

questions.q: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two persons run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 10 + 8 = 18 m/s

Time taken to meet = Total track distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 1620 ÷ 18 = 90 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.

Alternate Method

Speed of Q = 8 m/s

Length of the track (Total Distance) = 1620 m

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1620 ÷ 18

⇒ Time taken to meet = 90 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the absolute difference of their individual speeds (|v₁ − v₂|).

Time to Meet at the Starting Point

The time taken for two persons to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by them to complete one full round.

Distinct Meeting Points

questions.q: Two different quantities of the same solution having ingredients A and B are stored in two different containers. In the first container, there are 252 litre of A and 441 litre of B. In the second container, the total quantity of the solution was 1188 litre. How much of the solution in the second container was made up of ingredient B?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of ingredients A and B in the solution = 252 : 441 = 4 : 7

Total parts of the solution = 4 + 7 = 11 parts

Quantity of B in the second container = (7 ÷ 11) × 1188 litre

Quantity of B = 7 × 108 = 756 litre

∴ The correct answer is 756 litre.

Alternate Method

Given:

First container quantity of A = 252 litre

First container quantity of B = 441 litre

Second container total solution = 1188 litre



Calculation:

⇒ Since the solution type is the same, the ratio of A to B is constant in both containers.

⇒ Ratio of A : B = 252 : 441

⇒ Dividing both values by their HCF (63), Ratio of A : B = 4 : 7

⇒ Total proportion parts = 4 + 7 = 11 parts

⇒ In the second container, 11 parts = 1188 litre

⇒ 1 part = 1188 ÷ 11 = 108 litre

⇒ Quantity of ingredient B = 7 parts = 7 × 108

⇒ Quantity of ingredient B = 756 litre

∴ The correct answer is 756 litre.

Additional Information

Ratio of Mixtures

When two different quantities of the exact same solution are evaluated, the ratio of their constituent ingredients remains perfectly constant across all volumes.

Unitary Method

To find the value of a specific ratio component, determine the value of one unit by dividing the total quantity by the sum of all ratio parts, then multiply by the required component's ratio value.

Simplifying Ratios

Always simplify large ratios to their lowest terms by finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) to make further mixture calculations faster and less prone to error.

questions.q: P and Q are two fixed points 10 cm apart, and R is a point on PQ such that PR = 6 cm. By what percentage is the length of QR decreased when the length of PR is increased by 5%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the total length PQ is fixed at 10 cm, the absolute increase in PR will exactly equal the absolute decrease in QR.

Increase in PR = 5% of 6 cm = 0.3 cm, so QR decreases by exactly 0.3 cm.

Initial length of QR = 10 − 6 = 4 cm.

Percentage decrease in QR = (0.3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 7.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total length PQ = 10 cm

Initial length PR = 6 cm

Percentage increase in PR = 5%



Formula Used:

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease in Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Initial length of QR = PQ − PR = 10 − 6 = 4 cm.

⇒ PR is increased by 5%, so New PR = 6 + (5% of 6) = 6 + 0.3 = 6.3 cm.

⇒ Since PQ is fixed at 10 cm, New QR = PQ − New PR = 10 − 6.3 = 3.7 cm.

⇒ Decrease in QR = Initial QR − New QR = 4 − 3.7 = 0.3 cm.

⇒ Percentage decrease in QR = (0.3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 7.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

Always calculate the percentage increase or decrease using the original (initial) base value: % Change = (Change ÷ Initial Value) × 100.

Constant Sum Property

When the sum of two components is strictly constant (such as segments of a fixed line), any absolute positive variation in one component precisely matches the absolute negative variation in the other.

Base Value Importance

Although the absolute change (0.3 cm) is identical for both segments PR and QR, their percentage changes differ (5% vs 7.5%) due to their different starting base values (6 cm and 4 cm).

⇒ The maximum frequency is 5, which corresponds to the age of 10.

⇒ Difference = Mean − Mode = 10 − 10 = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Mean

The mean is the average of a dataset, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set of data may have multiple modes or no mode at all.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal and perfectly aligned at the center.

Empirical Relationship

For moderately skewed distributions, the empirical formula is: Mode ≈ 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.q:
Ramesh sells rice at ₹36 per kg, which he purchased for ₹30 per kg. Moreover, he gives only 800 g of rice instead of 1 kg

while selling. Find the actual profit percentage of Ramesh.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Price ratio (CP : SP) = 30 : 36 = 5 : 6

Weight ratio (CP : SP) = 800 : 1000 = 4 : 5

Overall CP : SP = (5 × 4) : (6 × 5) = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3

Profit % = [(3 − 2) ÷ 2] × 100 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost price (CP) of 1 kg (1000 g) rice = ₹30

Selling price (SP) of rice = ₹36

Weight given to customer = 800 g

Formula Used:

Profit = SP − Actual CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100



Calculation:

⇒ Actual cost price (CP) of 800 g of rice = (30 ÷ 1000) × 800 = ₹24

⇒ Selling price (SP) of 800 g of rice (sold as 1 kg) = ₹36

⇒ Profit earned = SP − CP = 36 − 24 = ₹12

⇒ Actual Profit % = (12 ÷ 24) × 100 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a shopkeeper uses a false weight, the actual Cost Price (CP) is calculated based on the weight physically given to the customer, while the Selling Price (SP) is charged for the claimed weight.

Successive Percentage Method

Overall profit or loss can be calculated by combining the ratio of CP to SP for the price and the ratio of true weight given to the false weight claimed.

Profit and Loss Formula

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100. Always consider the actual investment of the dealer as the base (100%) for profit or loss calculations.

For a number to be divisible by 5, its last digit (y) must be 0 or 5.

For a number to be divisible by 8, it must be an even number, so y = 0.

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Calculations:

⇒ Divisibility by 5 implies that the unit digit y = 0 or 5.

⇒ Since any number divisible by 8 must be an even number, y cannot be 5.

⇒ Therefore, y = 0.

⇒ Now, checking the last three digits (4x0) for divisibility by 8 using the given options.

⇒ For x = 4 → 440 ÷ 8 = 55 (Divisible)

⇒ For x = 2 → 420 ÷ 8 = 52.5 (Not divisible)

∴ The correct answer is 4 and 0.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 8

A number is completely divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 4

A number is completely divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.q: A discount series of 10% and 16% on an invoice is the same as a single discount of:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The equivalent single discount for two successive discounts a% and b% is:

⇒ Equivalent Discount = a + b − (a × b) / 100

Here, a = 10 and b = 16

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 10 + 16 − (10 × 16) / 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 26 − 1.6 = 24.4%

∴ The correct answer is 24.4%.

Alternate Method

Given:

First discount = 10%

Second discount = 16%



Calculations:

⇒ Let Marked Price (MP) = 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount (10%) = 100 − 10 = 90

⇒ Price after 2nd discount (16%) = 90 − (16 / 100) × 90 = 90 − 14.4 = 75.6

⇒ Total Discount = MP − Selling Price (SP) = 100 − 75.6 = 24.4

⇒ Equivalent single discount percentage = 24.4%

∴ The correct answer is 24.4%.

Additional Information

Ratio Method for Successive Discounts

Convert each discount into a fraction (e.g., 10% = 1/10 ⇒ MP : SP = 10 : 9). Multiply the MP parts and SP parts separately to find the overall ratio, then calculate the total net discount percentage.

Three Successive Discounts

To find the equivalent discount for a%, b%, and c%, first apply the formula a + b − (ab / 100) to find an intermediate discount d%, then apply it again with d% and c%.

Customer vs Dealer Perspective

For a customer, a higher successive discount is better. Among different combinations with the same sum (e.g., 20% + 10% vs 25% + 5%), the one with the larger difference between the individual discounts gives a greater net discount.
